hints: Look closely at the drawing in stage K. The two chromosomes are single rods with a dot at one end, not X-shaped, so what does that tell you about sister chromatids?
Remember the order around the cycle: stage M has no visible chromosomes (decondensed chromatin), so it must be interphase where DNA replication happens. Work forwards and backwards from there.
walkthrough:
**Decode what stage K shows**

Look at the two chromosomes in stage K. They are each made of a single chromatid, not the X-shape of a replicated chromosome.

That means sister chromatids have already separated. This is anaphase of mitosis, after metaphase and before the cell divides.

**Decode what stage M shows**

Stage M says no chromosomes were visible. That means the chromatin is long, thin and decondensed.

This is interphase. It is the only time when DNA replication (S phase) can happen and when chromosomes are invisible.

**Put J, L and M in order**

Follow the arrows: M (interphase) -> J -> K (anaphase) -> L -> M (interphase).

J must take the cell from interphase into anaphase, so it includes spindle attachment at metaphase. L must take the cell from anaphase back to interphase, so it includes cytokinesis after telophase. M itself includes DNA replication. That matches row A.

options.A: Correct. J is spindle attachment leading to metaphase then anaphase K, L is cytokinesis returning to interphase, and M is interphase with DNA replication.
options.B: Incorrect. Stage M has no visible chromosomes so it cannot be cytokinesis of mitosis, it must be interphase with DNA replication.
options.C: Incorrect. J comes after interphase M, so J cannot be DNA replication, and L comes after anaphase K so it cannot be condensation.
options.D: Incorrect. This puts the events backwards. Cytokinesis must follow anaphase K, not come before it, and condensation must come before anaphase, not after interphase.
